title: Smartwatch low-heart-rate alert (<40 bpm) sends a 32-year-old woman to hospital, where ciprofloxacin is identified as the cause of her bradycardia and replaced
summary: A smartwatch alert for a heart rate under 40 bpm two days after discharge on ciprofloxacin led to an ED visit; telemetry showed 30-50 bpm, the antibiotic was switched and the rate normalized.
account: Cordova Sanchez, Chohan, Olatunde and White of SUNY Upstate Medical University, Syracuse, reported in the Journal of Investigative Medicine High Impact Case Reports (published 24 January 2022; the event date is not given, so the publication date is used) a 32-year-old woman seen two days after discharge from a hospital stay for cholangitis, during which she had an ERCP and was sent home on ciprofloxacin and metronidazole. She developed dizziness on minimal exertion, and her smartwatch triggered an alert for a sustained heart rate below 40 beats per minute, prompting her to attend an outside emergency department, where telemetry confirmed 30-50 bpm; she was transferred to the authors' hospital for cardiology evaluation. Her ECG showed sinus bradycardia at 51 bpm, against 66 bpm before the antibiotics; the procedural drugs given two days earlier have short half-lives and other work-up (blood tests, thyroid function, Lyme serology, drug screen, echocardiogram) was unremarkable. Ciprofloxacin was replaced with ceftriaxone and by the next day her heart rate was 60-70 bpm; she was discharged on cefpodoxime and metronidazole. The authors conclude ciprofloxacin was the likely cause and that early recognition of the bradycardia prevented a potential adverse event. The watch's brand and model are not stated; the authors describe wearable heart-rate detection generically as photoplethysmography.
purpose: Smartwatch low-heart-rate alerts are built to prompt the wearer to seek review; this alert was that purpose. The authors add that consumer wearables may surface less commonly reported medication side effects.
system: Smartwatch low-heart-rate alert (brand and model not stated)
developer: Not stated (the report does not name the device's maker)

ratings.reason: The alert led to recognition of symptomatic drug-induced bradycardia and a change of antibiotic, after which her heart rate normalized; the authors say a potential adverse event was prevented but document no event that was imminent.

ai_role.statement: The watch's sustained low-heart-rate alert, combined with her symptoms, is what the authors say prompted the hospital visit; telemetry confirmed the rate and clinicians identified ciprofloxacin by exclusion and re-challenge-free withdrawal. The threshold alert is a simple rule on a photoplethysmographic heart-rate estimate, and the brand is unknown, so no learned model can be credited.
